newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NAIL TO BUY NAFHOLD FOR 600 MLN RAND.
newsitem.headline: NAIL TO BUY NAFHOLD FOR 600 MLN RAND.

text.p: New Africa Investments Ltd (Nail) said on Monday it would buy the 32.7 percent of New Africa Finance Holdings Ltd it does not already own for 600.7 million rand and constitute it as a wholly-owned subsidiary.

It said the rationale for the acquisition stemmed from its acquisition in June of a further 5.6 percent interest in Metropolitan Life Ltd, increasing the Nail group's effective interest to 34.9 percent.
While Nail would have significant influence over Metlife, this level of interest did not warrant a separate listing of Nafhold, a financial services company , as previously contemplated.

In addition, African Merchant Bank (AMB), in which Nafhold holds a stake, had developed into a fully-fledged merchant bank which had achieved rapid earnings growth and planned a 300 million rand private placement to its shareholders.

"Accordingly, Nafhold intends distributing its entire interest in AMB to Nafhold shareholders in order to broaden the shareholder base of AMB prior to the separate listing of AMB on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange which is expected to take place no later than March 31 1998..."

Nail said that subsequent to the distribution, there would no longer be compelling reasons for Nafhold's separate existence and Nail intended to acquire the 32.7 percent stake so as to constitute Nafhold as a wholly-owned subsidiary.
In terms of the deal, Nail proposed to acquire all Nafhold shares in exchange for Nail "N" shares in the ratio of 426.86 new Nail "N" shares for evey Nafhold shares held.
Nail also detailed the terms of its recently announced rights issue.

It said it would raise 1.004 billion rand through the issue of 318.91 million new Nail "N" shares of 0.0102008864 cents each at a price of 315 cents per new Nail "N" share in the ratio of 75 new "N" shares for every 100 ordinary or "N" shares held.
The offer would apply to shareholders registered on August 15.
